label: late original-phase input (t>=6) of k/u/3/m/b/p/v/1/j after an l/r/i/n/s/a/x/g earlier
explanation: Fires almost only on the last few original-phase inputs of long sequences (96% of mass in the original phase, rate rising from t=4 to a peak at t=7-8; L=8-9 hold 88% of mass; to_go 0-1 hold 84%). The remaining 4% is a weak tail on the <DEL> step. Never fires in the copy phase or at t<=2. On top of position it acts like an additive mix of (a) which token is being input now (k, u, 3, m, b, p, v, 1, j raise the rate 1.7-4x; first occurrences 1.6x) and (b) which tokens came early in the sequence (l, r, i, n, s as first token give ~3x). Activations are strongest when all three line up, e.g. l l x 0 s t y [k] or r l r z f n d h [k]. No single conjunction captures it: the late-position condition alone gives recall 0.79 and mass 0.86 but precision 0.10. Adding the token conditions raises precision to about 0.3 and keeps mass recall around 0.72. Many late k/u/3 inputs without the right early context stay silent, and some moderate activations fall on other tokens.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: k, u, 3, m, b, p; least: g, r, i, n) and the first original token (most: l, r, i, s, a, n; least: t, u, k, 3); timing cues that raise it most: t=7, t=8, L=9 & t=8.
